Subject: HIPAA: BAA scope, PHI boundary, and deployment eligibility — follow-up

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the procurement side.

Summary of what we heard:
- You expect to send and receive PHI in the form of lab test results, radiology summaries, and patient identifiers tied to scheduling workflows.
- Allied Health requires a signed BAA before any PHI is processed.
- Preferred deployment modes for PHI workloads: Dedicated (customer-isolated GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on-prem). 
- You asked whether Redwood's hosted API can be used for PHI with additional controls (e.g., customer-managed KMS).

Immediate asks we agreed on:
1) I've attached our standard BAA template for your legal team to review ("BAA_Template_AlliedHealth.pdf"). Please flag any redlines.
2) Attached a blank security questionnaire — you mentioned your team could pre-fill the PHI-specific sections and return ("Allied_Security_Questionnaire_Partial.xlsx").
3) We will provide a short written note on deployment boundaries: what we consider "PHI-eligible" and which hosted configurations are permissible.

Clarifying notes from our side (to help legal/infosec triage quickly):
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant (controls report available on request). We will share the current SOC 2 report with the security team after an NDA.
- For PHI: we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted API is typically excluded for unredacted PHI unless a customized private tenancy + customer-managed encryption keys and contractual commitments are put in place — we can scope this if needed.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You: return the questionnaire with PHI scope indicated (expected by end of week).
- Allied legal: review BAA template and send redlines (aiming for next Tue).
- Redwood: internal sec/infra to validate the requested deployment option and produce a short tech note on PHI handling (target: 48 hours after we receive the completed questionnaire).
- Schedule a follow-up call with your security and infra folks — propose Thu 2026-03-25 or Fri 2026-03-26.

Please let me know if I missed anything. If the timeline above looks off, we can adjust.

Thanks,

Thanks Sara and Neha — tagging in a couple technical clarifications from infra/ops. Below is a concise mapping that your security team can use in the questionnaire or in the call.

1) Deployment options and PHI handling (high level):
- Dedicated (recommended): customer-dedicated GPU pools, network isolation, optional customer-managed KMS (we can bind keys at the tenant level). Suitable for multi-tenant clouds where we reserve capacity just for Allied.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control of network boundaries; if you require on-prem we can provide an appliance/air-gapped bundle. Best for highest compliance/regulatory constraints.
- Hosted API (standard): not recommended for unredacted PHI by default. Possible only if we provision a private tenancy and customer-managed encryption keys and if legal signs off on additional contractual clauses (we will need to document retention and access controls explicitly).

2) PHI processing boundary details we need from Allied to finalize architecture:
- Are any PHI items being stored long-term by Allied or is Redwood expected to persist tokens/outputs? (This affects retention clause in the BAA).
- Expected qps and payload sizes (average tokens/attachments per request) — impacts whether Dedicated burst capacity is required.
- Any third-party integrations that will receive PHI (e.g., S3 buckets in Allied account, EHR connectors).

3) Evidence & artifacts we can provide for the questionnaire:
- SOC 2 Type II report (available after NDA).
- Architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private deployment modes.
- Sample DB retention/rotation policy, access control matrix, and key management overview.

If Allied confirms Dedicated or Private, our security team will prepare a short implementation plan and an expected timeline (typically 2-4 weeks for Dedicated provisioning; Private/VPC timelines vary by networking work).

I’ll pick up the questionnaire once the Allied team returns the filled copy and will route anything that needs sec/legal review.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Infra | Redwood Inference
